sentences.text: Mr. Pathan, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant, submits that the claim was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs. 3 lakhs from the present respondents.

It was an injury claim, and even after producing material on record to show that the appellant sustained 20% permanent disability, the learned Tribunal cryptically granted a lump sum compensation of only Rs. 15,146/- to the appellant/claimant.

2. Mr. Chapalgaonkar, learned counsel for the Insurance Company, submits that no appeal has been filed by the Insurance Company raising any (2) 933 FA 818 OF 2014 legal ground, and as such, the matter pertains purely to the quantum of compensation.

Mr. Chapalgaonkar, in all fairness, agrees that the learned Tribunal ought to have applied appropriate parameters to award compensation that would be just and proportionate in light of the prevailing law.
On this point, Mr. Chapalgaonkar seeks time of two weeks to consult with the Insurance Company and consider whether an amicable settlement can be offered to the claimant.

3. Mr. Pathan, learned counsel for the claimant, has also fairly agreed to the proposal for settlement,
considering that the claim is of 2003.
4.
In view of this, list this matter on 15.10.2025 for further orders.
[AJIT B. KADETHANKAR, J.] PRW Shaikh Gulam Mustafa Abdul Qadeer vs Brijlal Tukaram Khurana (Died) Thr Lrs. ...
